titulo: Pronouns in the accusative and negation (kein and nicht): The pronouns in the accusative

aula.titulo: Pronouns in the accusative and negation (kein and nicht)
aula.objetivo: Replace the direct object with pronouns (ihn, sie, es, mich, dich…), negate nouns with «kein» and everything else with «nicht», and answer negative questions with «doch».

blocos.texto: Goal of the lesson. By the end of the four sessions, you negate sentences with nicht or kein without hesitating, know where to put the nicht and answer negative questions with doch or nein.

blocos.contexto: Jonas wants to go out with Camila, but she is busy.

linhas.ru: — Hallo Camila! Hast du heute Abend Zeit?
linhas.en: — Hi, Camila! Do you have time tonight?
linhas.audio: Hallo Camila! Hast du heute Abend Zeit?

linhas.ru: — Leider nicht. Ich habe keine Zeit, ich lerne noch.
linhas.en: — Unfortunately not. I do not have time, I am still studying.
linhas.audio: Leider nicht. Ich habe keine Zeit, ich lerne noch.

linhas.ru: — Morgen habe ich Zeit. Aber ich spiele nicht gut Fußball.
linhas.en: — Tomorrow I have time. But I do not play soccer well.
linhas.audio: Morgen habe ich Zeit. Aber ich spiele nicht gut Fußball.

linhas.ru: — Kein Problem! Wir spielen nicht Fußball, wir trinken Tee.
linhas.en: — No problem! We will not play soccer, we will have tea.
linhas.audio: Kein Problem! Wir spielen nicht Fußball, wir trinken Tee.

linhas.en: — Great! I am not an athlete.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: There is a second trap. English uses “not” (with “don't”) for everything: “I don't have a car. I don't live in Berlin.” German splits the job between two words, nicht and kein. And, like standard English, German does not double the negative: Ich habe nichts.Ich habe nie Zeit. Without nicht. STEP 2: is there an ein in the affirmative sentence? Replace it with kein. No ein? Use nicht.
blocos.comparacao: English has a single “not”, always tied to the verb (with “do”): “I do not live in Berlin. I do not have a car. I do not have time.” German divides the job between two words and does not put the negation in front of the verb.

tabela.english: I do not live in Berlin.
tabela.avoid: negates the verb or the place: nicht

tabela.english: I do not have a car.
tabela.avoid: negates a noun without an article or with ein: kein

blocos.titulo: The pronouns in the accusative, step by step
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the DIRECT OBJECT is what undergoes the action: in «Ich sehe den Mann», the one I see is «den Mann». STEP 2: so as not to repeat the word, we replace the object with a pronoun: «Ich sehe den Mann» → «Ich sehe ihn.» STEP 3: the pronoun follows the GENDER of the word replaced: «der Tisch» → «ihn»; «die Lampe» → «sie»; «das Buch» → «es»; «die Bücher» → «sie». STEP 4: for people, the pronouns for «I» and «you» change form: «ich» → «mich», «du» → «dich». STEP 5: watch out for «sie» (she, they) and «Sie» (you, formal): the context and the capital letter show which is which. Remember that only the masculine changes in the article (den); in the pronouns, all of them change: ich → mich, du → dich, er → ihn, wir → uns, ihr → euch.
blocos.comparacao: English also changes pronouns («I see him», «she sees me»), but uses «it» for every thing. In German each pronoun has its own accusative form, and for things the choice depends on the gender of the word: ihn, sie or es, where English has only «it».

exemplos.ru: Wo ist der Schlüssel? Ich suche ihn.
exemplos.pt: Where is the key? I am looking for it.

exemplos.ru: Wo ist die Tasche? Ich finde sie nicht.
exemplos.pt: Where is the bag? I cannot find it.

exemplos.ru: Das Buch ist gut. Ich lese es gern.
exemplos.pt: The book is good. I like reading it.

erros.motivo: The direct object requires the accusative.

blocos.enunciado: Replace the objects with pronouns out loud: «Ich sehe den Mann → Ich sehe ihn», with 5 sentences of your own.
Write the accusative of «der Mann», «die Frau», «das Kind» and «die Kinder», with the definite article.
